items.title: European CLO issuance and AAA spreads — September 2026
items.capture_method: search_web grounded summary (condensed analyst note; primary not opened)
items.query: European CLO issuance September 2026 AAA spread new issue refi reset
items.excerpt: European CLO issuance year-to-date through September 2026 reached €94.9bn across 229 deals. September totalled €10.7bn across 24 deals: new issue €7.6bn (17 deals) versus refi/reset €3.1bn, ending three months of repricing dominance. BofA forecasts full-year refi/reset of about €60bn. AAA new-issue spreads averaged 124 bps in September (128 bps in August); refi/reset AAA averaged 120 bps, the lowest of the year.

items.title: Altice International — unrestricted subsidiaries, default notice, New York action
items.capture_method: search_web grounded summary (condensed analyst note; primary not opened)
items.query: Altice International 2026 default notice secured creditors unrestricted subsidiaries New York lawsuit
items.excerpt: In November 2025 Altice International designated Altice Portugal and Altice Caribbean as unrestricted subsidiaries and raised €750m at 12% due 2029. On 14 July 2026 the 2028 secured group served a default notice; about €8bn of secured debt is involved. In October 2026 an action was filed in the New York Supreme Court. Roughly €3.1bn matures in 2027; bonds trade in the mid-to-low 60s.

items.title: Thames Water — liquidity runway, Class B TSA, consortium
items.capture_method: search_web grounded summary (condensed analyst note; primary not opened)
items.query: Thames Water October 2026 emergency funding Class B creditors transaction support agreement special administration
items.excerpt: Thames Water has drawn £2.65bn of its £3bn emergency facility; cash runs out late 2026 to early 2027. It is seeking a further £2.4bn to last into autumn 2027, raising dilution concerns among super-senior holders (including PIMCO). A Class B Transaction Support Agreement backed by more than 60% of the roughly £1bn Class B debt provides a full write-off in exchange for about 5.9% recovery via equity plus rights in a £150m equity raise. The London & Valley Water consortium (Elliott, Silver Point) proposes Lord Hutton as chair-designate and Mike McTighe as vice-chair. A deal requires Ofwat concessions; there is political pressure to trigger the Special Administration Regime.

items.title: Fitch — European leveraged loan default rate and Market Concern list
items.capture_method: search_web grounded summary (condensed analyst note; primary not opened)
items.query: Fitch European leveraged loan default rate September 2026 forecast Market Concern list
items.excerpt: Fitch's European leveraged loan trailing-twelve-month default rate rose to 3.6% in September 2026, from 2.7% in August and 2.0% at mid-year. In July Fitch raised its full-year 2026 forecast to 4.0-4.5% from 3.0-3.5%. The Market Concern list stands at 10.3-10.6%, the highest since early 2013. Repeat defaults and liability-management exercises are a driver.

items.title: Bank of England FPC — private credit, leveraged lending, AI capex financing
items.capture_method: search_web grounded summary (condensed analyst note; primary not opened)
items.query: Bank of England Financial Policy Committee 2026 private credit leveraged lending AI capex financing vulnerabilities
items.excerpt: The FPC keeps private credit and leveraged lending on its vulnerability list. AI-related capex is increasingly financed through private credit, leveraged finance and structured finance. Concerns include the maturity wall managed through amend-and-extend, opacity and layered leverage; the system-wide exploratory scenario (SWES) informs the analysis.

items.excerpt: Commentators distinguish PIK structured at origination from 'bad PIK' switched on after origination, which they treat as a shadow default. Stress is concentrated in 2021-22 vintages and in software/SaaS borrowers exposed to AI disruption. No quantified public series of bad-PIK incidence was found.
